notes:
CIRCUIT: three parallel branches strung between a top rail (y~325, x 362..650) and a bottom rail (y~628, x 355..650) which carries the single GND symbol. Left branch: 10 Ohm resistor R2 in series with the 0.1V source V5. Middle branch: 1mF capacitor C1 in series with an unlabelled resistor R3, and the bottom of that branch is where GND attaches. Right branch: 10mH inductor L0 in series with the 3mA current source I4. The large rectangle around everything is the drawn page border, not a conductor - the tracer correctly left it on no net and it touches nothing.

NET MAP:
  0  = bottom rail y~628 plus the GND stub at x~508: bottom of V5, bottom of R3, bottom of I4, GND6.
  n1 = top rail y~325: top lead of R2 (x~361), top lead of C1 (x~522, via site S2), top lead of L0 (x~649).
  n2 = right mid-branch, x~652, y 441..485: bottom lead of L0 to top lead of I4.
  n3 = middle mid-branch, x~518, y 429..482: bottom lead of C1 to top lead of R3.
  n4 = left mid-branch, x~356, y 466..511: bottom lead of R2 to top lead of V5.

SITE DECISIONS (both CRITICAL sites recorded explicitly):
  S2 (522,333) deg=3, dot=2.0, hop=0: a plain tee - the top rail runs left-right and the capacitor's lead drops away downward from it; nothing continues above the rail. One wire ending on another is a junction by definition, and the drafter thickened the corner slightly. Junction. The alternative would leave C1's top lead on a one-terminal net and break the parallel structure of the three branches.
  S11 (508,625) deg=5, dot=2.1, hop=2.1: the bottom rail crosses the middle branch here; the branch arrives from above (R3's bottom lead) and continues below into the GND symbol. Junction - all five branch stubs are one node. The reported hop=2.1 comes from the GND symbol's own horizontal bars sitting a few pixels below the rail, not from any drawn hop over the rail. Reading this as a crossing would separate the bottom rail from the GND symbol, leaving V5 and I4 with no return path to ground and leaving GND on a one-terminal net; that is electrically impossible, so junction is forced independently of the ink.
  Non-critical sites S4 (585,430), S6 (567,433) and S8 (705,538) are the handwritten '1mF' and '3 mA' labels brushing the capacitor box and the current-source box; left at default, they change nothing.

PORT FIXES (each of these four produced a one-terminal net in the tracer output - the classic value-label-stroke error):
  - C1.t1 was sitting on a stroke of the '1mF' text at (562,433); moved to p3 (519,429), the real bottom lead, which runs down to R3's top (wire 54, the same wire R3.t1 already uses).
  - R2.t1 was on the '10 Ohm' text at (322,433); moved to p2 (357,466), the real bottom lead, which runs down to V5's top (wire 46).
  - I4.t0 was on the '3' of '3 mA' at (695,531); moved to p4 (654,485), the real top lead, which runs up to L0's bottom (wire 45, the same wire L0.t1 already uses).
  - V5.t0 was on the 'V' of '0.1V' at (302,543); moved to p2 (354,511), the real top lead (wire 46).
  L0 and R3 already pointed at both real leads and were left alone. No three-terminal parts on this sheet, so no pin-order work.

CLASSES: all seven symbols match their drawn shapes - Inductor (coil, '10mH'), Capacitor (two parallel plates, '1mF'), two Resistors (zigzags; the left one is labelled '10 Ohm', the middle one carries no value), I-DC (circle with up arrow, '3 mA'), V-DC (circle with +/- bars, '0.1V'), GND. No re-classification.

UNRESOLVED: nothing. Every terminal lands on a wire that is unambiguous in the pixels; the final netlist is 7 components / 5 nets with no floating or single-terminal nodes.
